Subject: Billing for 3-year prepay - request for annual invoices

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the call earlier. Our CFO asked us to confirm the billing cadence for the proposed 3-year prepay. They prefer to receive one invoice per contracted year (Year 1, Year 2, Year 3) rather than a single upfront invoice covering the full term for internal budget alignment.

Two constraints from procurement:
- Accounting needs a clear invoice line for each fiscal year to map to their budgets.
- They still want the commercial benefit of a multi-year prepay discount applied at signing.

Can Redwood issue three annual invoices that reflect the agreed prepay discount but are billed at the start of each year? If not, what are the options (e.g., one upfront invoice with revenue recognition note, staged invoices, or split billing lines)?

We also need a simple schedule to attach to our PO. Can you send a proposed billing schedule and any finance language we should include?

Best,
Bethany Liu
Procurement Manager
Acme Health

Hi Bethany — thanks for laying this out clearly. Looping in Marissa (finance) and Laura (legal) to confirm what we can do operationally and any contract language needed.

High-level options we typically offer:
1) Annual invoices with prepay discount applied up front but invoiced pro rata each year (we'd invoice Year1 at signing with a credit posted to Years 2-3) — requires us to hold deferred revenue on our books until earned.
2) Single upfront invoice for the full prepay (simplest operationally) with an attached amortization schedule for your accounting team.
3) Staged invoicing: e.g., 50% Year1 at signing, 25% Year2 at first anniversary, 25% Year3 at second anniversary — can be tailored.

Marissa, can you confirm which of the above still meets ASC 606 / our rev-rec policies and any wording we should provide to Acme to make their auditors comfortable?

I will draft a billing schedule and a DocuSign-ready invoice option once finance confirms.

Thanks,

Hi Bethany / Rishi — finance here. I reviewed the commercial term and put together three practical approaches with tradeoffs; attached is a sample schedule (billing_schedule_proposal_2026.xlsx) and a redlined SOW showing the suggested billing language (SOW_redline_multiyr_v2.pdf).

Option A — Single upfront invoice (full prepay)
- How it works: One invoice at signing for the full committed amount with the agreed discount applied.
- Pros: Lowest operational overhead, immediate cash receipt.
- Cons: Acme's side: needs internal memo for budget mapping; Redwood will record deferred revenue and amortize monthly.
- Rev-rec guidance: We'll recognize revenue over the service period (monthly amortization) consistent with ASC 606. We can provide an amortization schedule for your auditors.

Option B — Annual invoices with discount applied across line items
- How it works: We generate three invoices at the start of each contract year. The discount is applied pro rata so the net economic benefit equals the prepay discount. Redwood would still need to treat the full economic benefit as part of a single contract for rev-rec; however, issuing invoices annually is operationally possible if Acme provides POs for each year and accepts the net pricing.
- Pros: Aligns with your fiscal-year budgets.
- Cons: More accounts receivable work for both sides and requires explicit PO references per invoice.

Option C — Hybrid staged approach (e.g., 60/20/20)
- How it works: Portion invoiced at signing, remainder split across anniversaries.
- Pros/Cons: Middle ground on cashflow and AR effort.

Practical note: For Acme's auditors, the important items are: (1) clear contract language stating the prepay discount and the service delivery period, (2) an amortization schedule showing revenue recognized each month, and (3) invoicing lines that map to the amortization schedule. We can include a simple accounting appendix in the SOW to make it straightforward for your accounting team.

Next steps I propose:
- Rishi: pick the preferred billing rhythm (A/B/C) with Bethany.
- If B or C: Acme to provide one PO per invoice year (or explicit PO numbers for each invoice).
- Redwood: we’ll prepare the invoice(s) and DocuSign envelope; attach the amortization schedule and attach a short accounting note.

Attachments: billing_schedule_proposal_2026.xlsx (proposed line-item split), SOW_redline_multiyr_v2.pdf (recommended contract wording).

Marissa Cole
Head of Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
